title: Record form: a `datetime` field's picker offers no way to choose the time — picking a day writes 00:00 (or keeps the old time), so hours can only be typed by hand
body:
eval#1 · os-bob · session_012dn2AcTB69pEwZ9ugr1g1w

Filing gate: ① product defect, reproduced on a public entry (the Console record form) in the `os-dev-test` environment while building a leave-request app over MCP. ⛔ Not a claim; triage decides lane and grade.

### Edition
Not sure (seen in the `os-dev-test` environment's Console)

### Version
18.3.0 (Console)

### What happened / What you expected

**What happened.** On a record create/edit form, a `datetime` field renders the platform picker (`DateTimePickerField` → `TemporalPicker` with `withTime`). Its popover holds only a day calendar plus the "Today" / "Tomorrow" shortcuts — there is no hour/minute control. Picking a day writes `<day>T<time>` where `<time>` is the time already in the value, or `00:00` when the field is empty (`pickDay` in `ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/date-picker/DatePickerField.tsx`, `const time = nativeValue.slice(11, 16) || '00:00'`). The only way to set the hour is to type the whole value into the text box in the locale pattern (e.g. `2026/11/12 18:00`), which nothing on the form tells the user.

Observed on a leave-request form (zh-CN): the start/end are `datetime` fields; choosing 12 Nov in the calendar for "结束时间" produced `2026/11/12 00:00`, and the user could not find any way to pick 18:00 — they reported the field as "cannot select a time".

**What I expected.** The `datetime` face of the picker lets the user choose the time as well as the day, without typing:
- a time control in the popover (hour + minute; a configurable step such as 30 min would suit most business forms), and
- picking a day keeps the chosen time (current behaviour) and an empty value gets a sensible default rather than midnight — or at least the time control is focused next so midnight is not silently committed.

The `date` face (`withTime={false}`) is unaffected and should stay as it is.

### Steps
1. Define an object with a `datetime` field (e.g. `start_at: { type: 'datetime' }`) and open its create form in the Console.
2. Click the calendar icon on the field.
3. Observe: only a month grid and "Today" / "Tomorrow" — no time selector.
4. Pick any day → the input shows `<day> 00:00`.
5. The only way to get e.g. 18:00 is to type `YYYY/MM/DD 18:00` into the text box.

### Notes
- Code: `ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/date-picker/DatePickerField.tsx` — `DateTimePickerField` / `TemporalPicker`, the `PopoverContent` holds `<Calendar mode="single" …/>` and the two shortcut buttons only; `pickDay` and `shortcut` both fall back to `00:00`.
- Same widget is what `getLazyFieldWidget` hands action-param and bulk-action dialogs, so those surfaces have the same gap.

## Filing notes

- Business reason: any form with a `datetime` field (leave, overtime, meetings, bookings) cannot record a time without typing the whole value; users read it as "cannot choose a time".
- Reader who acts: the `ui/` fields seat (`ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/date-picker/DatePickerField.tsx`).
- Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue datetime picker time` and `DatePickerField time` (open and closed) → 20 + 3 hits; closest #26579 (screen-flow date input) and #27483 (invalid typed date), neither is the missing time control.
